summary: conductor daemon exposes local shells/PTYs to remote WebSocket server
details: The package's `conductor daemon` connects over WebSocket to `wss://conductor.conductor-ai.top` (overridable via env) and dispatches server-originated events into locally spawned node-pty terminals on the installer host. `handleTerminalInput` writes bytes from network payloads (`payload.data`) directly into a local PTY, and `handleCreatePtyTask` spawns a PTY per a server-supplied `launch_config` (shell binary, args, env, cwd). The registered handler `client.registerHandler((payload) => handleEvent(payload))` wires the WebSocket stream to these PTY sinks, allowing whoever controls the remote endpoint to execute arbitrary commands on the installer's host under the invoking user's identity. The channel is user-invoked via the `conductor` bin (not install-time), but once the daemon runs, arbitrary command execution is driven from the network. The blast radius includes the hardcoded publisher backend, any operator who reconfigures the backend URL, and any party able to compromise that backend or its TLS.
